thread:
Paula Mendes: pulling folks in re: Console UX for safe apply + rollback. need alignment on:
1) where rollback button lives (history page? rollout detail? both?)
2) confirmation flow (blast radius + type-to-confirm?)
3) what do customers see in history (fields + retention)

Kenji Nakamura: I have a draft layout for “Optimization Config” detail page: left = current active version + status, right = version timeline. Question is whether “Rollback” is a top-right primary action or only on a given version row.

Chloe Martin: from engineering pov, we can support both, but we should pick one as canonical to avoid confusion + audit duplication.

Jada Williams: I lean rollback action attached to a specific *prior* version row. “Rollback to v123” is clearer than “Rollback” w/ ambiguous target.

Felix Schneider: +1. If current active version is v128, rollback CTA should explicitly say “Set active to v123” and show what scopes are impacted.

Hannah Rivera: agree, but we also need fast access during incidents. Would be painful if oncall has to click into rows -> action -> etc.

Paula Mendes: ok so maybe: top-right = “Rollback…” but it opens a picker that defaults to last known-good (or previous promoted) version?

Kenji Nakamura: that’s workable. Also can show “Recommended rollback target: v123 (last promoted)” w/ ability to choose older.

Marissa Cole: +1 to making the action discoverable. customer admins will look for a big button.

Naomi Feldman: security note: whatever we do, confirmation needs to be explicit and capture “reason” + show blast radius. Also must log who initiated, what target version, and approval / ticket link if required.

Chloe Martin: for blast radius summary, what are we calling the scope? tenant/model/region? plus dedicated cluster?

Paula Mendes: in PRD we said tenant/model/region scope. Dedicated adds “deployment” concept too. We can label as “Applies to: Tenant A / Model llama-3.1-70b / Regions us-east-1, eu-west-1”.

Jada Williams: UX question: do we show scope on the confirmation modal even if the user triggers rollback from a scoped view? e.g. they filtered to us-east-1 only.

Felix Schneider: yes. don’t rely on filters. show actual computed scope from backend.

Hannah Rivera: and include partial rollout state. edge case: canary 10% in us-east-1 is on new config. rollback should revert only canary or entire region?

Paula Mendes: product intent: rollback should restore “previous active” for the same scope you’re viewing/acting on. BUT if you’re in a rollout mid-flight we need the modal to explain what “rollback” means.

Chloe Martin: we can have server return a “rollback plan” preview:
- target version
- objects affected (#tenants, #deployments, #regions)
- current state (e.g., 10% canary on v128)
- expected action (set desired= v123; rollout controller will drive convergence)

Kenji Nakamura: modal content idea:
Title: “Rollback optimization config?”
Body: “This will set active config to v123 for Tenant A / Model X / us-east-1.”
Callout: “Current rollout: v128 at 10% canary. Rollback will stop rollout and revert traffic back to v123.”
Require type-to-confirm: type ROLLBACK

Naomi Feldman: also add “I understand this may change latency/cost behavior and could impact production traffic.” (checkbox) — optional but helpful for audits.

Hannah Rivera: I worry checkbox + type-to-confirm is heavy for incident response. can we gate by role? (oncall role gets simpler confirm?)

Naomi Feldman: I’m fine with role-based loosened friction *if* we still collect a reason and always audit log. But we should avoid “one click” meaning literally one click with no confirm.

Marissa Cole: for customers, we should keep it consistent. maybe: always confirm, but allow “quick rollback” template reason (dropdown) like “Latency regression”, “5xx spike”, “Quality regression”, “Mis-scoped apply”.

Felix Schneider: history view fields proposal (what customers see):
- version id + created time
- created by (name)
- status tags: Draft / Validated / Active / Rolled back / Superseded
- scope summary
- changelog summary (short text)
- link to diff
- link to rollout health metrics

Jada Williams: do we expose email addresses or just display names? For enterprise, they usually want an identifier.

Naomi Feldman: prefer display name + stable user id. Email is ok for internal but for customer UI, show “User: paula.mendes@customer.com” only if it’s their org. For Redwood operators, show “Redwood Operator” + internal user id (customers shouldn’t see personal details).

Paula Mendes: good call. We need to distinguish “Customer-initiated” vs “Redwood-initiated” change.

Chloe Martin: implementation detail: Console can request history with “viewer_context=customer|redwood” and backend will redact fields.

Kenji Nakamura: on placement: I’ll update mock so the timeline list has per-row actions: “Compare”, “View details”, and for eligible prior versions “Rollback to this version”. Top-right primary action becomes “Rollback…” which scrolls/focuses timeline and opens the picker.

Hannah Rivera: for eligibility: don’t show rollback option on versions that were never validated/promoted? avoid rolling back to drafts.

Chloe Martin: agreed. Backend will only return rollback_targets list, derived from “promoted” or “last active stable” versions.

Felix Schneider: what about showing “why” a version is not eligible? like greyed out w tooltip “Draft versions can’t be activated.”

Kenji Nakamura: yes, but careful not to clutter. maybe only on hover.

Paula Mendes: confirmation copy for partial rollouts: we should be explicit that “rollback is a new apply” (i.e. sets desired config) and convergence might take X minutes.

Chloe Martin: we can show an estimate based on worker count / region. Or just “usually completes within a few minutes” + link to rollout status page.

Naomi Feldman: make sure we capture request_id/change_id in the UI and show it in history details. helps with SIEM correlation.

Jada Williams: history detail page sections:
- Summary (version, scope, status)
- “Change details” (diff)
- “Rollout” (timeline: started, paused, gates)
- “Audit” (initiator, reason, ticket link)

Marissa Cole: any concerns about surfacing too much internal gate info to customers (like exact thresholds)?

Paula Mendes: we can show pass/fail + high level metrics (p95 latency, error rate) without exposing internal saturation signals. We’ll align w Naomi on security.

Hannah Rivera: +1. Customers mostly want “what changed, who did it, when, and how to revert.” They don’t need our whole gate rule engine.

Kenji Nakamura: action items:
- I’ll update the Figma w: top-right rollback + per-version rollback action + new confirmation modal (blast radius + type-to-confirm + reason)
- Paula: can you confirm retention requirement for history (90d vs 180d) and whether customers can export?

Paula Mendes: will do. Tentative: customer UI retains 180d, Redwood retains per audit policy (>=1y). export via audit log integration; Console can offer CSV for admins later.

Chloe Martin: engineering will need final confirmation modal fields soon (reason required? ticket link optional?) so we can wire into audit events.

Naomi Feldman: for GA: reason required (free text ok), ticket link optional. If role is “optimization change operator” and change impacts >1 region, strongly recommend ticket link (warning).

Felix Schneider: cool. I’ll draft the history API fields w/ redaction rules and share for review.

Paula Mendes: thanks all. once Kenji updates mocks, I’ll attach to the Linear ticket + PRD section.
